statuses.stable: Supported for production use; incompatible changes require a semver-major release.
statuses.experimental: Published experimental APIs may continue to evolve, but receive the same semver protection as stable APIs until formally deprecated and removed.

new-component-experimental.rationale: This newly scaffolded component is an unreleased public-surface candidate whose API is still under maintainer review.
new-component-experimental.graduationCriteria: Graduate to stable only after its documented API, populated accessibility state, three-engine behavior, and compatibility contract pass review and a release qualification.

published-stable.rationale: This exact lr-* tag appears in a published Lyra release manifest and remains a supported public contract under semver.
published-stable.graduationCriteria: Already stable; it retains that status while its documented behavior, accessibility, compatibility, and cross-browser support remain part of the public contract.

published-experimental.rationale: This exact tag already appears in published Lyra versions and remains experimental under full semver protection while its public API and usage patterns mature.
published-experimental.graduationCriteria: Eligible for stable status once its documented API, populated accessibility states, cross-browser behavior, and compatibility contract demonstrate sustained reliability.

mapped-experimental.rationale: This implementation reinstates an earlier Lyra tag with the experimental Web Awesome 3.11 public surface and remains experimental while production usage is gathered.
mapped-experimental.graduationCriteria: Eligible for stable status once the mapped public surface, populated accessibility states, cross-browser behavior, and virtualization edge cases demonstrate sustained reliability.

introduced-mapped-experimental.rationale: This newly introduced Lyra tag mirrors an experimental Web Awesome 3.11 public surface and remains experimental while production compatibility evidence is gathered.
introduced-mapped-experimental.graduationCriteria: Eligible for stable status once the mapped public surface, populated accessibility states, cross-browser media behavior, and lifecycle edge cases demonstrate sustained reliability.

compatibility-stable.rationale: This tag preserves the previously shipped native time-control contract while the primary lr-time-input name provides the segmented control.
compatibility-stable.graduationCriteria: This compatibility surface remains stable while it preserves the Lyra 7 native behavior and has not entered a separately announced deprecation period.

introduced-stable.rationale: This tag entered Lyra as a stable public API with documented behavior, accessibility, and cross-browser support.
introduced-stable.graduationCriteria: Already stable; it retains that status while its documented behavior, accessibility, compatibility, and cross-browser support remain part of the public contract.

deprecations.name: base
deprecations.rationale: The accordion-item part names the outer wrapper explicitly; base remains on that same node during the compatibility window. That version is a policy floor, not a plan: Web Awesome still publishes its own deprecated `base` part on `wa-accordion-item`, and a mirrored tag owes its whole upstream surface, so this alias is removed only when upstream's is.

Neither pinned wa-split-panel nor sl-split-panel publishes a wrapper part, so base, the root part name used across the library, remains the single supported spelling. The removal-not-before version is a policy floor, not a plan: should either upstream publish a component-named wrapper part, this alias stays for as long as upstream ships it.

exportDeprecations.rationale: This tag-shaped route registers the deprecated lr-geojson-view alias (and, through it, lr-geojson-viewer). Import the lr-geojson-viewer route instead; this one keeps working unchanged through the 22.x line.

exportDeprecations.name: ./components/viewers/geojson-view/geojson-view.class.js
exportDeprecations.rationale: This route exists for the deprecated LyraGeojsonView alias class and its event map; its re-exports of LyraGeoJsonViewer and its types duplicate the canonical geojson-viewer class route. Import from that route instead; this one keeps working unchanged through the 22.x line.

exportDeprecations.name: ./components/viewers/geojson-view/geojson-view.js
exportDeprecations.rationale: This route registers the deprecated lr-geojson-view alias and, as a side effect, lr-geojson-viewer. Import the geojson-viewer route to register the canonical tag alone; this one keeps working unchanged through the 22.x line.

exportDeprecations.name: ./utilities/localization.js
exportDeprecations.rationale: The side-effect-free localization.js entry now re-exports every binding of this route (bridgeLyraLocale, resolveLyraScopedString, subscribeLyraLocale and the LyraLocaleBridgeOptions/LyraLocaleBridgeCleanup types), identical at runtime and in type, so one entry point carries the whole application-facing locale runtime. Changing the import specifier is the entire migration; this route keeps working unchanged through the 22.x line.

exportDeprecations.name: LyraGraphLink
exportDeprecations.rationale: Graph connections are called edges across the graph components. LyraGraphEdge is the structurally identical interface, and each is assignable to the other.

exportDeprecations.name: DocumentFile
exportDeprecations.rationale: LyraDocumentFile is the structurally identical interface under the library's prefixed type naming, and each is assignable to the other. Exported signatures keep the unprefixed name until the removal, so no existing signature changes in a minor release.

exportDeprecations.name: DocumentRendererDefinition
exportDeprecations.rationale: LyraDocumentRendererDefinition is the same union under the library's prefixed type naming. Exported signatures keep the unprefixed name until the removal, so no existing signature changes in a minor release.

exportDeprecations.name: LyraGeojsonViewEventMap
exportDeprecations.rationale: The event contract of the deprecated lr-geojson-view alias is exactly LyraGeoJsonViewerEventMap under a second name. The alias type keeps resolving to it, from this route and the package root, through the 22.x line.
